verdict: M1356 correctly pins the runner, M1350/M1353 identities, five fresh one-shot namespaces and the exact nine-key all-false claim boundary, but its contract checker ignores the declared one_shot, resource_fail_close and receipt_contract objects. Thirty of thirty non-control semantic mutations were accepted, including changed attempt/result namespaces and automatic_retry=true. The zero-false-negative launch-authority gate therefore fails.

failure_classes: complete one_shot object including attempt/result namespace and retry/cardinality

root_cause: validate_contract checks the exact identity dict and exact claim boundary, but only selected authorization/future_blind values; it never exact-compares one_shot, resource_fail_close or receipt_contract. Direct runner inspection currently proves the actual bytes are safe, but the requested reusable launch-authority contract is not an exact-set/value authority.
minimum_successor: Add an exact top-level key set/date gate and exact equality for one_shot, resource_fail_close, receipt_contract, authorization, future_blind, claim_boundary and protected_files. Add one regression for every M1357 false negative and obtain a fresh different-author zero-FN hammer. Preserve the runner bytes unless intentionally re-bound.
